evidence: Workbook Quality Checks!21 says the reference must be a committed static baseline with no nondeterminism on a pinned value. The frozen solution/solve.sh:4-6 resolves the shipped app directory and checks server.js; lines 8-35 guard an existing database before replacement; lines 37-38 remove only the old SQLite files and copy the shipped app. It has no install, build, generated source, or network fetch. The seed_data.json has an empty snippets array, and solution/app/server.js:142-169 creates schema but seeds no variable rows at boot. The shipped public/index.html points to local, prebuilt /assets files. My read-only hash check (per-row-review/evidence/20/reference-check.json) compared all 16 frozen solution files with HEAD commit dabcf7400a5c8b55fac5b71cd229a43035548961 and the live project source: all match. All 15 app files also match the expected hashes in the indexed exact-current full-install binding; the binding reports all_solution_files_match=true and health 200. The binding and local-proof-summary artifact SHA256s match the raw-evidence-index. Package-lock.json has integrity hashes for all 168 resolved entries, and solve.sh does not fetch them. A plausible broken reference could fetch or rebuild a different asset at solve time while still looking correct in source; this one copies fixed bytes. A conforming playground can use fresh per-action nonces and elapsed-time measurements without changing pinned content: app.tsx:44,78 and runtime.ts:24,312-330,379 use random IDs for console keys, retry identity, and run isolation. server.js:71,84,111 records wall-clock times for user-initiated saves/restores, but these do not seed content or determine any exact title, filename, source, revision, or graded figure; no public requirement or criterion pins a calendar value. This is source and scripted-install evidence for this row, not a configured Oracle, target-model, full judge, or portal grade.
